report:
Based on my research, the evidence actually suggests the answer is **yes** — monk's pepper (Vitex agnus-castus, also called chasteberry) does appear to help reduce PMS symptoms, contrary to your initial view.

**Key evidence:**

A **2017 systematic review** of 17 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) found that Vitex agnus-castus preparations were effective for PMS and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), outperforming magnesium, pyridoxine, and performing comparably to fluoxetine for some symptoms ([ScienceDirect, 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002937817303198); [NUNM summary](https://nunm.edu/2019/05/chaste-tree-berry-pms/)).

A **2019 meta-analysis** specifically evaluated properly characterized Vitex preparations and concluded they were effective in alleviating PMS symptoms ([ScienceDirect, 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229919306053)).

Clinical trials summarized by the **American Academy of Family Physicians** showed chasteberry reduced breast tenderness, irritability, depressed mood, anger, headache, bloating, and constipation ([AAFP](https://www.aafp.org/afp/2005/0901/p821)).

A **Springer review** noted that Vitex has been used commercially for 50 years for premenstrual symptoms, particularly mastodynia (breast pain), with most studies showing benefit ([Springer, 2017](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40816-016-0038-z)).

**Caveats:** Many trials have methodological limitations (small sample sizes, heterogeneous preparations). The mechanism likely involves prolactin modulation. Side effects are generally mild (nausea, headache, skin reactions). No Cochrane review was identified specifically for this topic.

**Conclusion:** The weight of evidence from multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses supports that standardized monk's pepper extracts can reduce PMS symptoms, particularly breast tenderness, mood symptoms, and physical discomfort. Your initial answer of "no" is not supported by the current literature.
